q: What combined horizontal-and-vertical sunshade blocks sun from many angles?
n: An egg-crate shade combines horizontal and vertical elements, blocking sun from many angles. Source: Olgyay, Solar Control and Shading Devices.

q: Emissivity is a material's ability to:
n: Emissivity is a material's ability to shed (radiate) heat. High-emissivity roofs radiate absorbed heat away and stay cooler, while low-e coatings on glass reduce heat transfer. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals.

q: In the Philippines, which side of a building gets direct sun for about eight months?
n: At Philippine latitudes (5–20° N), the sun is south of overhead for most of the year, about eight months, so the south side gets direct sun longest. Source: PAGASA; Olgyay, Solar Control and Shading Devices (sun-path diagrams).

q: In a hot-dry climate, what improves indoor comfort?
o: Smaller openings to keep out heat
n: In hot-dry climates, small openings and thick walls keep daytime heat out and improve comfort. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: Which does NOT create air movement inside a building?
n: High ceilings, large windows and cross ventilation all affect indoor air movement. A rough floor does not. Source: Givoni, Climate Considerations in Building and Urban Design.

q: What would you best recommend to improve cross ventilation, considering it is an open plan and cost?
o: Put heat insulation on the walls and the roof
n: In an open plan, enlarging the windows is the most cost-effective way to raise cross-ventilation airflow. Source: Givoni; DOE Guidelines on Energy Conserving Design of Buildings.

q: Besides temperature, what most improves indoor comfort?
n: After temperature, air movement most improves comfort in the humid tropics, by speeding evaporation from the skin. Source: Givoni; ASHRAE Standard 55 (elevated air speed).

q: What produces the most indoor airflow?
n: Large windows on opposite walls (inlet and outlet) give the most indoor airflow through cross ventilation. Source: Givoni, Climate Considerations in Building and Urban Design.

q: How should you best design the building to maximize natural airflow?
o: Introduce wide window and door openings
Integrate a mechanical vent in the attic to keep off contaminated air and draw in natural air
Make use of sliding windows instead of awning or jalousie windows
Minimize the use of AC systems
n: Wide window and door openings, placed for cross ventilation, maximize natural airflow without mechanical systems. Source: Givoni; DOE Guidelines on Energy Conserving Design.

q: What makes air feel hot in a hot climate?
n: Low wind speed makes hot air feel hotter, because still air limits evaporative and convective cooling of the body. Source: ASHRAE Standard 55; Givoni.

q: What is the minimum ceiling height of a naturally ventilated room in the Philippines?
n: A naturally ventilated first-storey room needs a ceiling height of at least 2.70 m. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 805.

q: Which window setup cannot circulate air through a room?
n: One window alone has no separate outlet, so it cannot drive air through a room. Source: Givoni, Climate Considerations in Building and Urban Design.

q: What's the best thing to provide to serve as a natural buffer on the southwest orientation?
n: Broad-canopied trees shade the southwest wall from hot afternoon sun and filter wind, a natural buffer. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: Which climate has milder overheating but high humidity that limits evaporation, with little day–night swing?
n: The warm-humid climate has moderate overheating, but high humidity limits evaporation, with little day–night swing. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: In the tropics, where should service cores go to shade the building?
n: Placing service cores on the east and west sides shields the occupied floors from low-angle sun. Source: Yeang, The Skyscraper Bioclimatically Considered.

q: Which is the least likely reason a tropical interior is hot?
n: Lack of insulation, small windows and no shade trees all make interiors hot. Paver spacing outside barely matters. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: On an east–west site, which side is most shaded through the day?
n: With the sun mostly to the south, the north side of an east–west building is the most shaded through the day. Source: Olgyay, Solar Control and Shading Devices.

q: In view of daylighting, room accommodations, corridors, and entrances should orient towards which direction?
n: North light gives even, glare-free daylight, so rooms, corridors and entrances are best oriented north. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (daylighting); Koenigsberger et al.

q: Which statement about tropical shading and ventilation is NOT true?
o: Transitional spaces go on the north and south where sun is weaker
The tropics need both vertical and horizontal shading
Maximum ventilation is generally wanted in the tropics
Transitional spaces need full climate control
n: In the tropics, transitional spaces (verandas, lanais) are meant to be naturally ventilated, so "they need full climate control" is false. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: Which statement about tropical heat gain is NOT true?
o: Heat gain is highest at low wind speeds
Tropical heat gain is mainly solar radiation on surfaces
Relative humidity in the tropics is very low
n: Tropical relative humidity is high, not low, so that statement is false. Source: PAGASA, Climate of the Philippines; Koenigsberger et al.

q: What is the best way to minimize glare in a building?
o: Put a canopy above the window
n: A canopy or overhang above the window blocks direct sky and sun glare while keeping the view. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (daylighting and glare); Olgyay.

q: To keep a master bedroom from overheating, where should it NOT go?
n: The west side takes the hot afternoon sun, so the master bedroom should not go there. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: Where are sun baffles normally applied?
o: Where the building is most exposed to sun
n: Sun baffles go where the building is most exposed to the sun. Source: Olgyay, Solar Control and Shading Devices.

q: Not considering natural ventilation and energy efficiency, what type of window should be placed on the west side of the building?
n: Leaving aside ventilation, the west wall is best kept solid, a plain wall used for cabinets or storage, to avoid afternoon heat gain. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: What natural sun buffer is best on a site?
n: Broad-canopied trees are the best natural sun buffer on a site. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; US EPA, Heat Island Reduction.

q: What tree is safe to plant near a public market and gives a tropical feel?
n: Palms have compact, fibrous roots that do not heave pavements, and they give a tropical character, so they are safe near a public market. Source: DPWH/UP Diliman landscape guidelines; arboriculture references (palm root systems).

q: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, what did millennials rank as the most serious global issue?
n: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, millennials ranked climate change and destruction of nature as the most serious global issue (48.8%). Source: World Economic Forum, Global Shapers Survey 2017.

q: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, where did government accountability and corruption rank among the top 10 global issues?
n: Government accountability, transparency and corruption ranked 6th (22.7%) in the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017. Source: World Economic Forum, Global Shapers Survey 2017.

q: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, what ranked 4th among the most serious global issues?
n: Poverty ranked 4th (29.2%) in the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017. Source: World Economic Forum, Global Shapers Survey 2017.

q: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, where did lack of economic opportunity and employment rank among the top 10 global issues?
n: Lack of economic opportunity and employment ranked 10th (12.1%) in the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017. Source: World Economic Forum, Global Shapers Survey 2017.

q: In the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017, where did safety, security and well-being rank among the top 10 global issues?
n: Safety, security and well-being ranked 9th (14.1%) in the WEF Global Shapers Survey 2017. Source: World Economic Forum, Global Shapers Survey 2017.
